Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Adult with 3–4 months of painful, cracked, intermittently itchy palmar skin; occasional bleeding only after scratching. Significant functional impact (off work 3 days). Strong temporal association with new hotel housekeeping job and frequent exposure to cleaning agents with inconsistent glove use. E45 emollient and an oral antihistamine were ineffective. PMH notable for type 2 diabetes.
- Most likely diagnosis: Irritant contact hand dermatitis due to occupational “wet work” and chemical exposure (DDx: High likelihood). Diabetes may contribute to xerosis and impaired skin barrier.
- Additional considerations: Allergic contact dermatitis to cleaning agents or glove components (DDx: Moderate likelihood) and asteatotic/xerotic eczema related to diabetes and baseline dry skin (DDx: Moderate likelihood).
- Less likely: Dyshidrotic eczema (no vesicles reported) and tinea manuum (no typical features) per DDx.
- No contradictions between transcript and DDx identified.

Management Plan
- Avoid triggers/irritants; wear protective gloves at all times during cleaning tasks.
- Prescribed steroid cream (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Use stronger emollients liberally 3–4 times daily for the next couple of weeks.
- Follow-up in 10–14 days if not improving, or sooner if worsening/spreading.
- Prescription sent to the patient’s pharmacy.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Irritant contact hand dermatitis (High): Onset after new housekeeping job; frequent exposure to cleaning chemicals and wet work; inconsistent glove use; palmar pain, cracking, and itch typical.
- Allergic contact dermatitis to occupational agents (Moderate): Exposure to potential allergens in cleaning products/gloves; pruritic chronic hand dermatitis; may coexist with irritant dermatitis.
- Asteatotic/xerotic eczema (Moderate): Baseline generalized dry skin and diabetes may impair barrier and healing, contributing to fissuring; distribution/localization favors contact dermatitis as primary driver.
